title: Learning and Practice
content_zh:
The Master said: "Is it not a joy to learn and practice what you have learned?"
The Master said: "Is it not a delight to have friends come from afar?"
The Master said: "Is it not gentlemanly not to take offense when others fail to appreciate you?"
Master You said: "A man who respects his parents and elders
is seldom inclined to defy his superiors.
And a man who never defies his superiors
never foments rebellion.
The gentleman works on the root.
Once the root is established, the Way grows."
The Master said: "Clever words and a pleasing countenance
are seldom associated with true virtue."
Zengzi said: "Every day I examine myself on three points:
In planning for others, have I been loyal?
In interacting with friends, have I been trustworthy?
And have I practiced what was taught to me?"
The Master said: "To guide a state of a thousand chariots:
Be attentive to affairs, and trustworthy.
Be frugal in expenditures and love the people.
And employ the common people only at the proper season."
